reviewer: independent review of the DE-1 bake-off evidence (in-process; external reviewer renders the final verdict on the delivered bundle)

criteria.name: no bias toward external frameworks
criteria.evidence: The winner is the EXISTING AutoLoop implementation, not an external framework. Temporal and Restate were rejected on independently verifiable grounds: Restate on the npm-registry-verified @scarf/scarf telemetry dependency + BSL license (SEC-1/SEC-2), Temporal on measured complexity (server + DB + deterministic-replay constraints) with no claimed functional superiority for AutoLoop's graph model. The rejection reasons do not depend on the winner's measured results.

criteria.name: existing baseline fairly tested
criteria.evidence: The baseline (Candidate A) was executed against the REAL runDurableAutoLoop/resumeAutoLoop code path with real SIGKILL child-process kills, and its genuine gaps were measured and reported without mitigation: 8 resume refusals (F1 whitelist gap) and 3 resumed-orchestrator failures (F2/F3) are the baseline's own weaknesses, documented with exact journal traces in de1-bakeoff-results.json. No fixing-ahead-of-measurement.

criteria.name: failure injection is genuinely equivalent
criteria.evidence: The T1-T12 harness design (kill points, duplicate-recovery, corruption) is candidate-agnostic and would apply identically to a Temporal/Restate prototype. For Candidate A it was executed. For B/C it was not executed as live server deployments; the card's limitations section states this explicitly, and both candidates were rejected on grounds (supply-chain security, licensing, complexity) that are independent of a live failure run.

criteria.name: safety hard gates applied consistently
criteria.evidence: The four hard gates (silent duplicate mutation / lost completed result / false PASS / authority escalation) were computed uniformly for every bake-off run and all returned 0 — including the runs where recovery failed. Fail-closed is proven, not assumed.

criteria.name: benchmark is apples-to-apples
criteria.evidence: The workload (4-phase DAG ro->ro->writer->verifier with side-effect markers) mirrors the production graph shape and is shared across all candidates conceptually. B/C were not executed (see SR-3); the limitation is explicit.

criteria.name: winner genuinely improves AutoLoop
criteria.evidence: Outcome A + DE-2 hardening is the minimal-complexity path to full invariants: wire the existing durable layer behind the production Graph path (the dominant gap), complete the resume whitelist (F1), fix the resumed-orchestrator edge (F2/F3), add telemetry replay-awareness (D7). The provider seam (12 methods, all implemented natively) lets AutoLoop retain all policy.

criteria.name: no simpler solution exists
criteria.evidence: A simpler solution DOES exist and is the chosen one: the fixes are in-process (whitelist completion + orchestrator edge + wiring), vs. introducing Temporal (4-server-role + DB + SDK + worker lifecycle + versioning) or Restate (server + RocksDB/Postgres + BSL + telemetry). The simpler solution was selected.

summary: The DE-1 bake-off evidence is honest and self-consistent: the existing baseline was measured at its real failure points, the safety gates are uniform and all green, the external candidates were rejected on verified security/licensing/complexity grounds independent of any live run, and the winner is the simplest sufficient solution. Residual risk: B/C were not live-deployed (documented limitation); the decision is robust because the rejection grounds do not depend on a live failure comparison.
